definitions.explanation: A type of saltwater clam found along the coasts of Japan, China, and Korea. Valued as a food ingredient and culturally significant as a symbol at the Doll Festival.

examples.japanese: ハマグリの{味噌汁|みそしる}を{作|つく}る。
{潮干狩|しおひが}りでハマグリを{取|と}った。
ひな{祭|まつ}りにはハマグリの{吸|す}い{物|もの}を{食|た}べる{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: There is a custom of eating clam soup on the Doll Festival.

notes:
Can also be written in kanji as {蛤|はまぐり}, but the katakana form ハマグリ is standard in modern usage, especially in menus, recipes, and everyday writing. The name comes from {浜|はま} (beach) and {栗|ぐり} (chestnut), referring to the chestnut-like shape of the shell.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ハマグリの{味噌汁|みそしる}: clam miso soup
- ハマグリの{吸|す}い{物|もの}: clear clam soup
- ハマグリの{酒蒸|さかむ}し: sake-steamed clams
- {焼|や}きハマグリ: grilled clams

CULTURAL NOTE:
ハマグリ is traditionally served at ひな{祭|まつ}り (the Doll Festival, March 3) because each pair of clam shells fits only with its original partner, symbolizing a faithful marriage. The shell-matching game {貝合|かいあ}わせ also uses clam shells.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- アサリ: short-necked clam — smaller and more common; used in pasta and miso soup
- シジミ: freshwater clam — tiny clams used in miso soup, associated with liver health
